batch_strategy: local response curves with targeted V2-tail repair, loading contrasts, and chemically matched controls

choices.reason: Low-strength m125 anchor predicted at 5.37/11.79 ml. It brackets the strong m125 tail seen at 5c2bc1d92128a17d996d and c4b5a5499258f39b7ac1, while extending the low end beyond 55f2352b50967352163e.

m125 at 1/1 with 50 ul sample volume and 500 ul loading solvent is predicted at 10.92/35.34 ml. This tests whether the tail begins before the large high-strength response, using 55f2352b50967352163e and 03744855d469f4cca7e6 as nearby measured anchors.

m125 at 2/1 and high loading-solvent volume is predicted at 20.66/41.42 ml. It fills the strength transition between the compact and broad measured m125 regimes and separates a real V2 expansion from a global shift.

m125 at 5/1 with only 50 ul sample volume is predicted at 37.77/70.22 ml. Comparing this point with measured 74cf50c6ec476a394b01 and c4b5a5499258f39b7ac1 tests whether the tail persists when loading amount is reduced.
Low-strength m177 anchor predicted at 4.10/11.94 ml. It provides the compact baseline needed to interpret the long finishes at b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 5b706e17e8412d02342f.
m177 at 10/1 and 50 ul sample volume is predicted at 3.16/12.43 ml. This probes the onset of the finish-tail transition between measured 27bac953781c17a3a74b and the much later b514312eda7950cdcf1c.
m177 at 20/1 with 150 ul sample volume is predicted at 2.55/13.28 ml. It supplies a strength and loading contrast for the unusual separation between onset and finish observed in b514312eda7950cdcf1c.
Low-strength m96 point predicted at 5.92/8.56 ml. It anchors the nonlinear m96 response before the broad measured behavior at a3c817ff559d5c946cc8 and 5bad82a6cffd60e7a6c9.
m96 at 2/1 is predicted at 8.36/11.52 ml and tests the early part of the onset-to-finish transition, complementing measured a3c817ff559d5c946cc8 and 4b4d079fa6b12df47a35.
m96 at 20/1 and 100 ul sample volume is predicted at 21.73/31.64 ml. It directly calibrates the intermediate V2 regime between the compact and high-strength measured m96 points.
m96 at 50/1 and 100 ul sample volume is predicted at 28.21/47.80 ml. This is a loading contrast to the measured 5bad82a6cffd60e7a6c9 point and tests whether the finish tail scales with sample amount.
m118 at 1/1 with 150 ul sample volume is predicted at 6.13/16.44 ml. It supplies a moderate loading anchor between the compact measured 0afe12e53e575503e3f0 and the later m118 regimes.

m118 at 10/1 and 150 ul sample volume is predicted at 8.56/24.00 ml. It tests the local strength transition against measured 319e89d7000731f64e7f, 2d178efe0181baca2bd5, and 24a9086a8e2c8015c232, which show strongly condition-dependent finishes.

Low-strength m146 point predicted at 8.36/18.05 ml. It extends the measured low-strength baseline from 8e999302c4d108ec9f19 before the large high-strength responses in 9e3ce3497298084abd83 and 23ef03f3e75e40b20095.
m146 at 1/1 and 50 ul sample volume is predicted at 9.64/24.72 ml. This probes the beginning of the late heteroaromatic response and calibrates V2 directly against 8e999302c4d108ec9f19.

The same m146 1/1 condition with 150 ul sample volume is predicted at 9.61/24.72 ml. The matched ratio and altered loading amount provide a direct loading test for a family whose measured tail grows strongly with condition, including 61b73b8065ae2ece22eb.
m141 at 5/1 and 100 ul sample volume is predicted at 17.59/41.68 ml. It fills the transition toward the measured late m141 behavior in 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 and 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0.

m141 at 10/1 and 100 ul sample volume is predicted at 27.84/65.89 ml. Together with the 5/1 point, it tests whether this scaffold has a distinct strength-dependent tail rather than inheriting a generic aromatic correction.
Low-to-intermediate m159 point predicted at 5.89/14.19 ml. It anchors the severe measured m159 transition between d3d2b36ec3417c1c1c6c, 59d8c3d932aece6945ae, and the extreme a17bcdddcf0799baeee2.

m159 at 1/1 and 50 ul sample volume is predicted at 4.81/11.27 ml. This compact local anchor helps identify where the very late response begins and limits indiscriminate correction of carbonyl-rich rows.

Low-strength m160 point predicted at 5.59/11.66 ml. It supplies a baseline for the donor/acceptor-rich loading response measured in 537a64f15ea470d73b03, b21061720e23b7a5bdcb, and ad833f34f6b91872362d.

m160 at 1/1 and 50 ul sample volume is predicted at 7.20/18.70 ml. This local contrast tests whether the severe m160 tail is activated by strength before the high-loading failures in ad833f34f6b91872362d.

m209 at 20/1 with 150 ul sample volume is predicted at 16.58/47.99 ml. It is a loading contrast to the 50 ul point and to measured bd3435c0f9b14ec7997d, testing whether the donor-containing tail is amount-dependent.

Matched m209 20/1 point with 50 ul sample volume is predicted at 16.61/47.98 ml. Pairing it with the 150 ul point can separate loading effects from the established strength response in 534afc6bd39a8f7923d8 and 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf.

m209 at 50/1 and 100 ul sample volume is predicted at 27.70/79.86 ml. It extends the local curve toward the measured long finish in 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf and tests direct V2 calibration at the upper-strength end.

Novel bromoacetophenone-like m43 at 10/1 is predicted at 6.03/14.20 ml. This donor-free halogenated control tests whether tail corrections spill into ordinary carbonyl chemistry, using the ordinary controls 3588135cce392e640236, 742735a20e3a21be6d2c, and 72ab072149ea3aa635af.

Ordinary ester m85 at 1/1 is predicted at 5.33/9.55 ml. It is a compact central-distribution control against the broad predicted intervals targeted elsewhere and complements measured b8c7bb9f7fff1a3e3f7d and 1a462e0cc4fc1474a76c.

High-strength donor-free anisole m126 is predicted at 6.85/13.09 ml. It checks whether family-specific tail repair leaves simple ether rows centered, complementing measured e7b3f786a783fb44ea83 and 638920730c17fcaca9ca.

Donor-free m214 at 20/1 is predicted at 6.63/12.05 ml with a broad V2 width. This chemically distinct control tests whether uncertainty and tail corrections generalize to hydrophobic diaryl chemistry without donors.

Compact nitrile-containing m130 at 0/1 is predicted at 6.26/13.66 ml. It provides an acceptor-only control for overcorrection of ordinary rows, alongside measured 63cda70afb5b740e4fa4 and 65d07ddf4c4bdb3cf60b.

High-volume m95 at 2/1 is predicted at 9.99/22.50 ml with a broad V2 width. It tests whether loading volume alone produces a real finish expansion in a less extreme carbonyl scaffold, complementing the measured high-loading behavior in 8d018e521e8e6bbc53c2.

Compact m23 ester control at 1/1 is predicted at 4.29/8.25 ml. It anchors the central V1/V2 distribution against the strong late-tail candidates and complements measured 1a462e0cc4fc1474a76c and fae79bab43155a52988f.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response and onset/finish coupling remain scaffold-specific, with transition locations and slopes that cannot be represented reliably by one global PE/EA trend.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local same-molecule strength curves teach scaffold-conditioned transitions and slopes for both V1 and V2, reducing inappropriate global solvent corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do transition locations transfer within functional-group families, or must they remain scaffold-specific?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume alter V1 and V2 differently across scaffolds, so mass alone is insufficient as a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts help the retrained model distinguish loading-driven onset shifts from finish-tail expansion and avoid folding both into solvent or molecular descriptors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA ratio, does loading primarily shift onset, expand finish, or change both in a scaffold-dependent way?

hypotheses.content: V2 and interval width require direct local calibration; predicted quantile width is useful for finding probes but is not a generally calibrated estimate of finish-tail behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct V2 labels across compact, intermediate, and broad predicted regimes can teach the model when a wide interval reflects a real chromatographic tail.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can structural descriptors predict finish width across families, or are local scaffold-condition anchors required?

hypotheses.content: Late-retention failures cluster across heteroatom-rich, carbonyl-rich, heteroaromatic, and multifunctional scaffolds, but their transition locations remain local.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Sampling multiple late-response families lets retraining learn transferable structural signals while preserving family-specific transition locations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which local structural environments best identify a scaffold's transition into late V2 behavior?

hypotheses.content: Novelty alone is insufficient; donor-free, halogenated, and compact acceptor-only controls are needed to constrain overcorrection of ordinary rows.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Ordinary controls protect overall Row-distribution accuracy while tail repairs are learned in the failure regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After tail repair, do ordinary donor-free and compact acceptor-only rows remain centered across strength and loading regimes?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes strengthened the case for local response curves and family-specific tails. m172 moved from a compact measured point at 1/1 in 6cb56f71f524d68d7e3f to a much later measured point at 50/1 in 419f6eb4080dcb9d293b. The measured m96 point a3c817ff559d5c946cc8 remained compact despite a broad prediction, confirming that quantile width is not a calibrated tail probability. The m73 result 2cf789c87f7c6325c020 exposed a large central-distribution failure outside the main late families. The long finishes in b514312eda7950cdcf1c, e4fd83fb3852eb354a66, and c4b5a5499258f39b7ac1 continue to support direct V2 repair, while their different onset behavior argues against transferring one correction globally.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates several scientifically meaningful local curves: m125, m177, m96, m118, m146, and m141 cover weak-to-strong transitions or loading contrasts in families with measured tail failures. m159 and m160 supply low and intermediate anchors for severe multifunctional and donor/acceptor-rich responses, while m209 tests loading dependence within a donor-containing curve. The remaining m43, m85, m126, m130, m214, m95, and m23 rows are compact or donor-free controls spanning carbonyl, ether, nitrile, halogenated, and diaryl chemistry. Together these measurements repair direct V2 behavior, distinguish solvent response from loading effects, and constrain overcorrection of ordinary rows across the Row-distribution.
